notes: Hermes synchronous no-LLM slash commands (/help, /status). Hermes' Source is ProcessOwnedStore (no transcript files at all — one shared SQLite store at $HERMES_HOME/state.db, core/adapters/inbound/agents/hermes/agent.go), so a proc-<PID> pre-session is born ready when `hermes chat` launches and the store-backed session (id <YYYYMMDD>_<HHMMSS>_<hex>) only appears once the first real turn creates its row (run_agent.py _ensure_db_session is called from the turn path). The warm-up turn is therefore mandatory, not decoration: it is what materializes the row the slash window is asserted against. Post-birth phases anchor to warm_turn_start rather than to the birth, because a proc- pre-session never goes working — templated from the verified opencode sibling. After warm_turn_end returns to ready, slash_window pins the SAME store-backed session ready for duration_at_least_ms:6000 with invariants forbidding state_transition to working/waiting — those are what would fire if /help or /status (incorrectly) drove a model call. They cannot: the REPL intercepts /-prefixed input at cli.py:15755 and dispatches it through process_command without it ever entering conversation_history, so no messages row is written (confirmed against the live store: zero rows with content LIKE '/%' across 117 rows of real use), and the watcher's reconcile emits EventActivity only when message_count grows or ended_at flips. Observations: model is pinned from the live surface (config.yaml model.default and 18 of 25 live sessions), cost is asserted non-zero only — Hermes reports estimated_cost_usd=0.0 under billing_mode='subscription_included', so irrlicht prices it from capacity/aliases.go.
